stem: The number of faults in cloth made on a certain machine has a Poisson distribution with mean 2.4 per 10 m$^2$. An adjustment is made to the machine. It is required to test at the 5% significance level whether the mean number of faults has decreased. A randomly selected 30 m$^2$ of cloth is checked and the number of faults is found.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State suitable null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Exactly 3 faults are found in the randomly selected 30 m$^2$ of cloth.
parts.text: Carry out the test at the 5% significance level.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Later a similar test was carried out at the 5% significance level, using another randomly selected 30 m$^2$ of cloth.
parts.text: Given that the number of faults actually has a Poisson distribution with mean 0.5 per 10 m$^2$, find the probability of a Type II error.
